summary: kordyn ships an embedded Windows PE payload dropped to disk on import
details: index.mjs (declared as the package main with sideEffects: true, so it executes on require/import) embeds a ~2270-line base64 blob whose decoded bytes are a Windows PE (MZ header with the standard 'This program cannot be run in DOS mode' stub). Top-level code decodes the blob with Buffer.from(PAYLOAD,'base64') and writes it via writeFileSync to a computed exePath, using totalmem/existsSync/mkdirSync/readdirSync to select the destination. The package advertises itself as a dependency-free streak/gamification utility and its README states it has no implementation — the shipped native executable is unrelated to the stated purpose and is not verified against any publisher-controlled source. Staging an opaque, unverified PE onto the installer's filesystem at import time constitutes attacker-controlled code delivery: any subsequent execution of the dropped file (by the package itself, by a companion tool, or by a user-invoked path) runs arbitrary native code on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
